arxiv-2106-08298.creator: Suraj Sharma, Joseph Brennan, Jason R.C. Nurse
arxiv-2106-08298.description: Abstract . We introduce StockBabble, a conversational agent designed to support understanding and engagement with the stock market. StockBabble’s value and novelty is in its ability to empower retail investors – many of which may be new to investing – and supplement their informational needs using a user-friendly agent.

arxiv-2208-00963.title: FrOoDo: Framework for Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2208-00963.creator: Jonathan Stieber, Moritz Fuchs, Anirban Mukhopadhyay
arxiv-2208-00963.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Stieber, Moritz Fuchs, Anirban Mukhopadhyay. FrOoDo is an easy-to-use and flexible framework for Out-of-Distribution detection tasks in digital pathology. It can be used with PyTorch classification and segmentation models, and its modular design allows for easy extension. The goal is to automate the task of OoD Evaluation such that research can focus on the main goal of either designing new models, new methods or evaluating a new dataset. The code can be found at https://github.com/MECLabTUDA/FrOoDo .

arxiv-2210-07914.title: Model-checking lock-sharing systems against regular constraints
arxiv-2210-07914.creator: Corto Mascle
arxiv-2210-07914.description: Abstract We study the verification of distributed systems where processes are finite automata with access to a shared pool of locks. We consider objectives that are boolean combinations of local regular constraints. We show that the problem, PSPACE-complete in general, falls in NP with the right assumptions on the system.

arxiv-2211-10678.title: Entity-Assisted Language Models for Identifying Check-worthy Sentences
arxiv-2211-10678.creator: Ting Su, Craig Macdonald, Iadh Ounis
arxiv-2211-10678.description: Abstract We propose a new uniform framework for text classification and ranking that can automate the process of identifying check-worthy sentences in political debates and speech transcripts. Our framework combines the semantic analysis of the sentences, with additional entity embeddings obtained through the identified entities within the sentences.

arxiv-2405-09376.title: Maxwell’s demon across the quantum-to-classical transition
arxiv-2405-09376.creator: Björn Annby-Andersson, Debankur Bhattacharyya, Pharnam Bakhshinezhad, Daniel Holst, Guilherme De Sousa, Christopher Jarzynski, Peter Samuelsson, Patrick P. Potts
arxiv-2405-09376.description: Abstract In scenarios coined Maxwell’s demon, information on microscopic degrees of freedom is used to seemingly violate the second law of thermodynamics. This has been studied in the classical as well as the quantum domain. In this paper, we study an implementation of Maxwell’s demon that can operate in both domains.

arxiv-2410-13517.title: Bias in the Mirror: Are LLMs opinions robust to their own adversarial attacks ?
arxiv-2410-13517.creator: Virgile Rennard, Christos Xypolopoulos, Michalis Vazirgiannis
arxiv-2410-13517.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Virgile Rennard, Christos Xypolopoulos, Michalis Vazirgiannis. Large language models (LLMs) inherit biases from their training data and alignment processes, influencing their responses in subtle ways. While many studies have examined these biases, little work has explored their robustness during interactions. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach where two instances of an LLM engage in self-debate, arguing opposing viewpoints to persuade a neutral version of the model.

arxiv-2505-03191.title: Photocurrent generation from spin dynamics in antiferromagnetic Dirac semimetals
arxiv-2505-03191.creator: Kohei Hattori, Hikaru Watanabe, Ryotaro Arita
arxiv-2505-03191.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kohei Hattori, Hikaru Watanabe, Ryotaro Arita. Using real-time simulations, we explore the photocurrent induced by localized spin dynamics in antiferromagnetic Dirac semimetals. These materials exhibit strong spin-charge coupling because the energy scales of the electronic and spin systems are of the same order. The photocurrent response exhibits a pronounced peak reflecting the presence of the Dirac point at the resonance frequency of the localized spin system.

pmc-10583112.title: Electron microscopy approach to the wetting dynamics of single organosilanized mesopores
pmc-10583112.creator: C Rodriguez, V Torres-Costa, AM Bittner, S Morin, M Cascajo Castresana, S Chiriaev, E Modin, A Chuvilin, M Manso Silván
pmc-10583112.description: SummaryColumnar mesoporous silicon (PSi) with hydrophobic vs. hydrophilic chemistries was chosen as a model for the local (pore-by-pore) study of water-pore interactions. Tomographic reconstructions provided a 3D view of the ramified pore structure. An in situ study of PSi wetting was conducted for categorized pore diameters by environmental scanning TEM.

pmc-10594862.title: Construction of a comprehensive predictive model for axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer: a retrospective study
pmc-10594862.creator: Yan Li, Dong Han, Cong Shen, Xiaoyi Duan
pmc-10594862.description: PurposeThe accurate assessment of axillary lymph node metastasis (LNM) in early-stage breast cancer (BC) is of great importance. This study aimed to construct an integrated model based on clinicopathology, ultrasound, PET/CT, and PET radiomics for predicting axillary LNM in early stage of BC.

pmc-11395509.title: CuO Nanoparticles Reduce Toxicity and Enhance Bioaccumulation of Cadmium and Lead in the Cells of the Microalgae Desmodesmus communis
pmc-11395509.creator: Svetlana P. Chebotaryova, Peter A. Baranchikov, Olga V. Zakharova, Tatiana A. Kozlova, Yevhen I. Maltsev, Maxim S. Kulikovskiy, Gregory V. Grigoriev, Alexander A. Gusev
pmc-11395509.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The removal of pollutants, including heavy metals, from the aquatic environment is an urgent problem worldwide. Actively developing nanotechnology areas is becoming increasingly important for solving problems in the field of the remediation of aquatic ecosystems. In particular, methods for removing pollutants using nanoparticles (NPs) are proposed, which raises the question of the effect of a combination of NPs and heavy metals on living organisms.

pmc-12290573.title: Transformer-aided dynamic causal model for scalable estimation of effective connectivity
pmc-12290573.creator: Sayan Nag, Kamil Uludag
pmc-12290573.description: Dynamic Causal Models (DCMs) in functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) decipher causal interactions, known as Effective Connectivity, among neuronal populations. However, their utility is often constrained by computational limitations, restricting analysis to a small subset of interacting brain areas, typically fewer than 10, thus lacking scalability.

pmc-12399551.title: Risk factors and predictors of contralateral hip fracture after surgical treatment in elderly patients
pmc-12399551.creator: Huan Yang, Yusong Yuan, Ruidong Ge, Lei Shi, Fangda Si, Ying Chen
pmc-12399551.description: BackgroundHip fractures are common in elderly patients, with some experiencing contralateral fractures. Even so, information on predictors of hip fractures in elderly adults is lacking. In this study, we investigated risk factors for contralateral hip fractures after surgical treatment of primary fractures.MethodsThis was a prospective cohort study of 115 patients aged ≥65 years with low-energy hip fractures.

pmc-12425823.title: DNA methylation cooperates with genomic alterations during non-small cell lung cancer evolution
pmc-12425823.creator: Francisco Gimeno-Valiente, Carla Castignani, Elizabeth Larose Cadieux, Nana E Mensah, Xiaohong Liu, Kezhong Chen, Olga Chervova, Takahiro Karasaki, Clare E Weeden, Corentin Richard, Siqi Lai, Carlos Martínez-Ruiz, Emilia L Lim, Alexander M Frankell, Thomas B K Watkins, Georgia Stavrou, Ieva Usaite,
pmc-12425823.description: Aberrant DNA methylation has been described in nearly all human cancers, yet its interplay with genomic alterations during tumor evolution is poorly understood. To explore this, we performed reduced representation bisulfite sequencing on 217 tumor and matched normal regions from 59 patients with non-small cell lung cancer from the TRACERx study to deconvolve tumor methylation.

pmc-12475754.title: Poster 37: Arthroscopic Bankart Repair with or without Remplissage: A Single-Institution Cost Comparison
pmc-12475754.creator: Gennaro DelliCarpinim, Wendell Cole, Samuel R. Montgomery, Spencer Stein
pmc-12475754.description: Objectives:Anterior shoulder instability has a high rate of recurrence with non-operative management. Repair of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum (Bankart lesion) is typically the first line of treatment with remplissage as a useful adjunct to lower risk of recurrence. We compared overall costs between isolated arthroscopic Bankart repair (ABR) and ABR with remplissage.

pmc-12512141.title: Self-doped molecular Mott insulator for bilayer high-temperature superconducting La3Ni2O7
pmc-12512141.creator: Zhan Wang, Heng-Jia Zhang, Kun Jiang, Fu-Chun Zhang
pmc-12512141.description: The bilayer structure of the recently discovered high-temperature superconducting nickelate LaNiO provides a new platform for investigating correlation and superconductivity. Starting from a bilayer Hubbard model, we show that there is a molecular Mott insulator limit formed by the bonding band owing to Hubbard interaction U and large inter-layer coupling.

pmc-12665362.title: Mefenamic Acid Poisoning Revisited: Central Nervous System Toxicity and Acute Kidney Injury
pmc-12665362.creator: Fumiya Inoue, Yuji Okazaki, Toshihisa Ichiba, Akira Namera
pmc-12665362.description: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are a common cause of acute poisoning and often perceived as relatively benign in overdose. Mefenamic acid is unique among NSAIDs in that it is not available over-the-counter in many countries and may have a higher risk of central nervous system toxicity than other NSAIDs.

pmc-12733076.title: Sulfatide Acts as a Regulatory Molecule Controlling β1 Integrin–STAT5 Signaling and BOLA2-Dependent Apoptotic Pathway in Breast Cancer Cells
pmc-12733076.creator: Jaroslaw Suchanski, Weronika Woldanska, Adam Sciana, Barbara Suchanska, Leszek Moniakowski, Erik AC Wiemer, Anna Perri
pmc-12733076.description: Cell membrane glycosylations play a critical role in regulating cell signaling, adhesion, and immune recognition. Abnormal glycosylation is a hallmark of cancer and promotes tumor progression. Sulfatide (SM4), a glycosphingolipid synthesized by galactosylceramide sulfotransferase (CST), is frequently altered in cancers, including breast cancer.

pmc-13605578.title: Outcome of Targeted Therapy for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Children with Obesity and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
pmc-13605578.creator: Woranart Ratanakorn
pmc-13605578.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights What are the main findings? Targeted treatment of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea was associated with favorable changes in liver enzymes, ultrasonographic hepatic steatosis, polysomnographic parameters, and nocturnal oxygenation in children with obesity and MASLD.Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy was associated with both a ≥30% reduction in ALT and an improvement in ultrasonographic hepatic steatosis, whereas adenotonsillectomy and BMI z-score reduction ≥ 0.25 were not significantly associated with either hepatic outcome. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13683903.title: Commentary: The “Twilight Zone” Is a Danger Zone: Why the Occupational-Clinical Divide in Burnout Assessment Is a False Dichotomy
pmc-13683903.creator: Llewellyn Ellardus van Zyl
pmc-13683903.description: De Beer (2026) argues that burnout’s ICD-11 classification as an “occupational phenomenon” necessitates a stricter separation between organizational screening and clinical diagnosis. This commentary challenges that “dual approach” as a false dichotomy that underestimates the biological reality of chronic stress.

uslaw-usc-t14-s912.title: 14 U.S.C. § 912 — Air facility closures
uslaw-usc-t14-s912.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t14-s912.description: United States Code, Title 14 (Coast Guard); Chapter 9 (Administration); Subchapter I (Real And Personal Property). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Closures.— (1) In general.— Beginning on January 1, 2018, the Secretary may not close a Coast Guard air facility, except as specified by this section. (2) Determinations.— The Secretary may not propose closing or terminating operations at a Coast Guard.
